sources.title: R. Bayly Winder, Saudi Arabia in the Nineteenth Century, London: Macmillan / New York: St. Martin's Press, 1965 (xiv+312 pp.) — the standard monograph on the second Saudi state.
Madawi al-Rasheed, A History of Saudi Arabia, Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 2002 (2nd ed. 2010) — history by a Saudi-born scholar, critical of official dynastic narratives.
Alexei Vassiliev, The History of Saudi Arabia, London: Saqi Books, 1998 (576 pp., ISBN 0-86356-935-8) — Russian-school historiography drawing on Arabic, Turkish and Russian sources.

ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh Ibn Bishr, ʿUnwān al-majd fī tārīkh Najd [The Sign of Glory in the History of Najd], vol. 2 completed 1270 AH / 1853-54 CE — contemporary Najdi chronicle covering the first and second Saudi states to 1854.
